The Nigerian Communications Commission and Financial Services Innovators have expanded efforts to improve women’s access to employment in the technology sector through a digital skills programme that has trained 95 female university students in Northern Nigeria, with 15 selected for industry internships. The eight-week software testing programme, sponsored by the NCC and implemented by FSI, attracted 590 applications from female students across Kano, Nasarawa, Bauchi, Sokoto and Katsina states, reflecting growing interest in technology careers among young women in the region. FSI disclosed in a statement on Monday that 115 students enrolled in the programme, which was held between 8 August and 26 September 2026. However, only 95 completed the mandatory assignments and practical tasks and were subsequently awarded final grades. The 15 successful candidates will begin five-week internships at GoAssurify Limited in November, where they will put their training into practice in a professional setting and acquire hands-on experience in software testing. The programme was designed to equip female students in tertiary institutions with technical competencies and industry exposure that could improve their prospects of securing employment in the digital economy. Participants received training in software testing principles, software development life cycle models, test case design, defect management, web application testing and application programming interface testing. The curriculum also included practical assignments and collaborative projects involving web and API testing simulations, with participants introduced to industry tools such as Jira and Postman. FSI said the initial six-week training schedule was extended by two weeks to give participants more time to complete practical assignments and accommodate those facing internet connectivity challenges and other learning barriers. Fifteen students were selected for internships, while six recorded scores of at least 70 per cent. Khadija Danhassan, a computer science student at the National Open University of Nigeria in Kano State, emerged as the programme’s top performer, scoring 93.5 per cent. The organisation noted that the programme attracted students from disciplines beyond computer science and other technology-related courses, demonstrating the potential for women from different academic backgrounds to pursue careers in the digital sector. Participants also came from nursing, biological and chemical sciences, mass communication, accounting, business administration, engineering, law and education. It requires giving them access to relevant skills, practical learning opportunities, industry mentors and clear pathways into the workplace,” she said. Kola-Oladejo said the receipt of 590 applications reflected the growing interest among young women in Northern Nigeria in exploring opportunities within the digital economy. She added that the completion of the programme by 95 students and the selection of 15 for internships represented progress in converting that interest into practical skills and employment opportunities. “With the support of the Nigerian Communications Commission, we are helping to turn that interest into practical capability and opportunity. Through our SmartGirls Initiative Africa, we want more young women to see themselves not just as users of technology, but as the professionals who test, develop, secure and build the digital solutions shaping our future,” she said. The software testing programme is part of FSI’s SmartGirls Initiative Africa, which seeks to reduce the gender gap in the technology industry through technical training, mentorship and industry exposure. The initiative focuses on four technology areas: artificial intelligence, software testing, software development and cybersecurity. Beyond technical instruction, the programme seeks to connect participants with industry professionals who can guide them on workplace expectations, career pathways and the competencies required to secure and retain technology jobs. FSI said the training also exposed persistent barriers to digital education, including unreliable internet connectivity, power supply interruptions and limited access to suitable devices. The organisation stated that insights gained from the programme would guide future initiatives aimed at enhancing accessibility and increasing enrolment in subsequent editions. It further disclosed plans to expand the SmartGirls Initiative Africa to reach more young women in Nigeria and across other African countries. FSI commended the NCC for sponsoring the programme and GoAssurify Limited for providing internship opportunities, alongside participating tertiary institutions, facilitators and peer volunteers who supported the training.
